ECO-COMS is a Workday Extend app: 40 pages and 45 cards in one hub ("ECO-COMS"), reading Workday through REST, WQL and the Graph API with the signed-in user's token. Every change goes through a guarded orchestration (13 orchestrations sharing 4 sub-orchestrations) that re-checks its inputs, calls Workday's Human_Resources or Staffing web service, confirms Workday accepted the change, and only then writes an audit record. Application formats, role requests, audit records and bulk runs are kept in five Extend business objects and two attachment stores; the organizations, roles and assignments themselves live only in Workday, where AccessUBC already reads them.

html:
Sequence for a single change (create organization, create pattern, change status, change role positions):

  • The page loads Workday data with the user's token: WQL (custom and top-level organizations, positions, assignable roles, academic units), REST (app business objects, /workers/me), Graph (audit records).
  • The user fills the form; scripts check each field against the rules (for patterns, the application's schema JSON on its COMS Application record).
  • On OK, onSubmit launches the orchestration through a deferred inbound endpoint (launch URL with URL-encoded parameters) as the user.
  • The orchestration re-checks every input that decides what changes (CheckInputs / CheckPatternName / CheckMode), calls the Workday web service (Organization_Add_Update, Organization_Inactivate, Reactivate_Organization, Assign_Roles), stops if the response is not 2xx or is a SOAP fault (CheckWWSAccepted), extracts the Workday event reference, and calls IORC_0037_XFD_SEC_Sub_Write_Audit_Record with the run ID.
  • The page re-reads Workday (the new code in WQL, or the audit record count +1) and either shows the receipt or blocks OK with "Workday rejected …".

Bulk changes: the grid writes its rows to COMS Bulk Row Result, the file upload stores a CSV in COMS Bulk Upload; an asynchronous orchestration (IORC_0037_XFD_SEC_Bulk_Role_Changes_From_Grid / IORC_0037_XFD_SEC_Bulk_Role_Changes_From_CSV) runs IORC_0037_XFD_SEC_Sub_Process_Bulk_Role_Row per row in VALIDATE or APPLY mode and updates COMS Bulk Run.

Role requests: the request is saved in COMS Assignable Role; IORC_0037_XFD_SEC_Start_Role_Request_Review / IORC_0037_XFD_SEC_Start_Admin_Request_Review (→ IORC_0037_XFD_SEC_Sub_Start_Request_Review) starts the Review COMS Assignable Role Request event as the requester and stores its WID; review step pages complete the steps; IORC_0037_XFD_SEC_Close_Denied_Role_Request runs on Deny or Cancel.

Reports: four model report data sources (ECO-COMS Role Requests, Audit Trail, Bulk Runs, Applications) for Workday custom reports.

rows: Is this a workaround for a platform constraint?
Partly: Workday has no delegated, bounded way to create custom organizations or a schema for their names; ECO-COMS provides it with guarded calls.
AccessUBC shell-role extract (unchanged), then the target applications
Does it create, change or delete records?
Creates custom organizations; changes their status; adds/removes positions on role assignments; creates app records (requests, audit, bulk runs, formats). Deletes nothing in Workday.
Organizations: inactivate (cannot delete). Role assignments: reversed by the opposite change (Assign Roles can't be rescinded). Requests: withdrawn/denied, not deleted once a review exists.
Why is this more appropriate than an EIB or core configuration?

Delegation to non-ISC users needs bounded, checked forms; an EIB or the standard tasks give no naming rules, no limit to an application's own org type, and show other roles. The bulk feature mirrors a Get/Put EIB inside those limits.

title: Diagram — Process workflow
html:
900ECO-COMS Role Request WorkflowECO-COMS Role Request Workflow1

Role request workflow: requester, ECO-COMS orchestrations and the Workday review business process, including deny, cancel and withdraw

Monday 3 Nov, Clockwork exam coordination needs access for CPSC 110 section 101 in 2026W2.

1. The Clockwork administrator searches "Shell Org Manager", picks Standalone → CLW. The Ready card shows the format "PATTERN: Academic Unit, Subject, Course, Section, Academic Period".

2. Add Pattern: CPSC · CPSC_V · 110 · 101 · 2026W2. Typing "cpsc_v" shows an error; corrected, the preview reads X:CLW:PATTERN:CPSC:CPSC_V:110:101:2026W2. Effective date: a weekday.

3. OK: IORC_0037_XFD_SEC_Create_Pattern_Shell_Org checks the prefix and five fields, IORC_0037_XFD_SEC_Sub_Create_Shell_Organization calls Organization_Add_Update under type X:CLW, subtype X:SHELL; Workday accepts; an audit record is written; the page finds the new code in WQL and shows "Pattern Created". Elapsed: a few seconds.

4. The administrator opens Manage Role Assignments for the Clockwork role on that organization, browses My Organizations → their department, picks the coordinator's position, OK. Assign_Roles runs; the audit record links to the Assign Roles event.

5. Overnight, AccessUBC extracts the new organization and assignment; Clockwork grants access for that section. No ISC ticket was raised.

6. In January the coordinator moves to another job. The position becomes vacant, so the next extract removes access; Access Review lists the shell role on the vacant position until someone confirms or removes it.

If step 3 had failed (e.g. the X:CLW organization type missing), the page would have shown "Workday rejected this request, so nothing was created" and no audit record would exist.
